Status report for the geom_slice overhaul requested in `dev_todo.Rmd`
("as robust, clean, and ggplot-native as geom_smooth, but far more transparent").
Updated as work progresses; latest entry first.

# 2026-07-07 — Full rewrite landed

`R/geom_slice.R` was rewritten from scratch (the old file's logic was not
salvageable in place; the SliceLayer instance-inheritance hack made every fix
fight ggplot2's plumbing). **All 32 `gs_` cases pass** — 26 visual cases were
checked one-by-one against their `testing/reference/` ground-truth images, and
the 6 console cases were re-snapshotted after review. A full 153-case run of
the whole suite shows no regressions (the 7 remaining FAILs are pre-existing
`KNOWN ISSUE` cases in `drawit`/`geom_fit`/`slice_2d`, which fail by design).

## Architecture (what replaced what)

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `SliceLayer` built *inside* `geom_slice()`, inheriting from a layer *instance*, with a hand-copied `compute_statistic` | One package-level `SliceLayer <- ggproto("SliceLayer", ggplot2:::Layer, ...)` passed via `layer(layer_class = )` (ggplot2 ≥ 3.5.0, already pinned in DESCRIPTION). Its only job: hand `computed_mapping` to the stat, then call the parent method. All group/panel/NA plumbing is inherited, which is what fixed grouping + faceting. |
| Variable names from `names(model$model)` (breaks on `I(x^2)`, `log(y)`) | Raw variables from the formula via `get_all_vars()` (`slice_model_frame()`), so transformed terms resolve to real columns for `predict()`. |
| `detect_response_transform` (string-ish, limited) | `get_inverse_function()` (already in the package, handles composed/binary transforms), wrapped by `resolve_y_fn()`. |
| Bare `stop()/warning()/message()`, inconsistent wording | `slice_abort()/slice_warn()/slice_inform()` everywhere, following the two-part what/hint format in `decisions.Rmd`. |
| Per-group imputation messages (would repeat per panel × group) | Slice plan resolved once per layer in `StatSlice$compute_layer` (`build_slice_spec()`); each imputation messages exactly once. |
| `dplyr::select/right_join/rename` dependency | Base R + rlang only (NAMESPACE trimmed; `%>%` kept for `geom_fit`). |

## How a slice is decided (the "transparency" contract)

For each model predictor, in priority order:

1. **`predict_vars`** value (validated at call time; wins over everything),
2. **group aesthetic** — an aes like `color = g` mapped to a single model
   predictor pins it to each group's own value (one line per group),
3. **facet variable** — pinned to each panel's value,
4. **imputed** — mean (numeric) / most common (factor, character), announced
   with a `slice_inform()` naming the value and a copy-pasteable
   `predict_vars = list(...)` hint.

The y side: `resolve_y_fn()` compares the model's response expression with the
plot's y-aes expression. Identical → predictions used as-is (`aes(x, log(y))`
with `lm(log(y) ~ x)` stays straight, gs_26). Same base variable, different
expression → invert the response transform (and apply the y-expression), with
an informative message. Different variable → `slice_warn()`. `back_transform`
overrides: `FALSE` (off), a 1-arg function, or a name ("log", "sqrt", ...).

Positional scales: the stat inverse-transforms panel x back to data units
before `predict()`, and forward-transforms predicted y — so `scale_x_log10()` /
`scale_y_log10()` (gs_24/25) now line up with the points.

Composite x-axis expressions (`aes(x * x_pos, y)`, `aes(log(x), y)`,
gs_19–23): predictions are evaluated at the model's own data rows (filtered to
the group), placed at each row's axis-expression value, sorted. `n` is ignored
in that mode.

## Errors now raised at *construction* time (clean, not stat-wrapped)

- non-`lm` model; `$` in variable names; unknown/response names in
  `predict_vars`; non-scalar `predict_vars` values; invalid `back_transform`
  (wrong type, unknown name, wrong arity); `n < 2`; an explicit `xaxis =`
  argument (slice_2d habit) gets a pointer to `aes()`.

All six `gs_2x` error-case snapshots were reviewed and updated accordingly.

## Test-suite touches

- `testing/expected/gs_27..32` re-snapshotted (old snapshots captured the
  broken behavior; `EXPECT:` headers described the desired behavior, which is
  what the new output matches).
- gs_16 header/labels said "first level (4)" but the reference *code* (and
  PNG) hold cyl at the mode ("8") — text fixed in the case and reference
  script, reference PNG regenerated (same line, corrected title).
- gs_15 `EXPECT` wrongly promised a "downward-sloping" line; the reference
  shows the true nearly-flat/slightly-rising partial slope — text fixed.

## Known caveats / follow-ups (also in `known_issues.Rmd`)

- `ggplot2:::Layer` is unexported → `R CMD check` note. Drop the `:::` if
  ggplot2 exports `Layer`.
- `group = var` (bare group aes) cannot pin `var` per group (ggplot2 turns
  group values into opaque ids before the stat) — geom_slice warns and
  imputes; use `color`/`linetype` instead.
- Roxygen was rewritten in-file, but `devtools::document()` has NOT been run
  (roxygen2 version mismatch churn — see the note at the bottom of
  `decisions.Rmd`). NAMESPACE was surgically trimmed (3 dplyr importFrom lines
  removed); exports unchanged. Next intentional `document()` run should
  reproduce it.
- Not done (queue items, unchanged): impute-method choice (min/max/median),
  confidence/prediction intervals, multiple-value `predict_vars` fan-out,
  data-vs-model mismatch check, `slice_*()` helpers rollout to `slice_2d`/
  `geom_fit`/`drawit`.
